title: Karna: the wheel stuck, the death
hook: Karna takes command, and asks for a king to hold his reins
tomorrow: Karna: the wheel stuck, the death

segments.voice: Your line was the ground itself took note. Bhishma is down, and now Drona too. Who do the Kauravas turn to now? Day eight hundred thirty-seven.

A new commander needs a driver. In the Kaurava camp, Duryodhana turns to his friend Karna and gives him the army. Karna accepts, and then he says something honest. Arjuna has an advantage I don't, he tells Duryodhana, in effect. Arjuna has Krishna holding his reins. If I'm to face him, I need a charioteer who knows horses the way Krishna does. And Karna names the man: Shalya, king of Madra, the uncle of the Pandava twins, who ended up fighting on the Kaurava side. Today, the ask, and the strange bargain behind it.
screen: `KARNA TAKES COMMAND.` → `ARJUNA HAS KRISHNA.` → `I NEED SHALYA.`

segments.voice: Duryodhana goes to Shalya and asks. And Shalya is furious. In Ganguli's English, the king takes it as an insult: he, a crowned king, told to drive for Karna, who was raised in a charioteer's house. He nearly walks out of the camp. So Duryodhana talks him round. He praises Shalya's skill with horses, he says Shalya is Krishna's equal at the reins, and he tells an old story of the gods, in which the creator Brahma himself drove the chariot for Shiva. Driving, in that story, is no shame. Shalya agrees, with one condition. He'll take the reins, but he'll say whatever he likes to Karna's face. Karna accepts. Here's the layer underneath. Before the war began, the epic tells us, Shalya met Yudhishthira and made him a promise. If he ever drove for Karna against Arjuna, he would wear down Karna's courage with his words. So the man now stepping into Karna's chariot carries a promise to the other side. Karna asked for a driver to match Krishna, and he got one. He also got a voice in his ear that was never quite his. The story doesn't hurry to tell us how that will go. It just lets the two men climb into the same chariot.
screen: `KARNA ASKS FOR SHALYA` · `A KING TOLD TO DRIVE` · `I WILL SAY WHAT I LIKE` · then, large: `A PROMISE TO THE OTHER SIDE`

segments.voice: Sit, and let your hands rest on your knees, loosely, like reins held without pulling. Breathe in slowly. Breathe out. Now notice the voices that ride along with you today, the ones in your head and the ones beside you. You don't have to answer any of them. Just notice whose voice is near the reins. Breathe in, and let your hands soften. Breathe out, and let the chariot stand still for a moment. If you pray, you can rest in prayer here. The bell holds the time.
Karna. The new commander of the Kauravas, who asks for a king to drive him, and gets a king who carries a promise to the other side.
Your line: a voice in his ear. Today, when someone offers to steer for you, ask quietly what they've already promised. Day eight hundred thirty-seven.

howItsDone: Hindus meet Karna's last battle through recitations and readings of the Mahabharata, retellings, regional theater and television serials; the Karna Parva, the epic's book named for him, tells this part of the war.

fork.setup: you're Shalya, a king, asked to drive the chariot of Karna, who grew up in a charioteer's house. what do you do?
options: agree, on condition you may speak your mind to Karna.
agree, and keep silent all the way.
fork.reveal: after nearly walking out, Shalya agrees, but only if he can say whatever he likes to Karna. Karna accepts.

original.note: charioteer: what Krishna is for Arjuna, and what Karna asks Shalya to be.

trapdoor: what you thought: a charioteer just drives the horses.
what it means: in the epic the charioteer rides close enough to advise, warn and steady the warrior, as Krishna does for Arjuna.
what a scholar hears: Karna was raised in a charioteer's house, so his request turns an old insult around: now a king must do the work Karna was mocked for.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Karna Parva, Karna made commander and his request for Shalya as charioteer; Shalya's anger, Duryodhana's persuasion (including the story of Brahma driving Shiva's chariot) and Shalya's condition
Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva, Shalya's promise to Yudhishthira to dishearten Karna

notes: Editor pass: cut the count 'second commander' from the review and the superlative 'the friend he trusts above everyone' from the hook; removed the stale note about day 836 (it does end with Drona's death).
All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli that Karna himself asks for Shalya, comparing him to Krishna as a judge of horses, and that Duryodhana tells the Tripura story with Brahma as Shiva's charioteer.
Confirm Shalya's condition (freedom to say what he likes to Karna) and that Karna accepts it.
Confirm the Udyoga Parva promise to Yudhishthira is described as wearing down or dampening Karna's spirit.

The word and carry are the index's ('Karna' / 'Karna: the wheel stuck, the death'); the carry has a capital (a name) and repeats across six days. A lowercase carry such as 'the wheel stuck' may read better; owner's call.
